page: Google Cloud Platform n2-standard-128 is a large-scale general-purpose virtual machine based on the x86_64 architecture. It features 128 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 64 physical cores across an Intel Xeon processor running at a base clock of 2.6 GHz, with 2 threads per core. Memory capacity totals 512.0 GB of RAM, maintaining a balanced 1:4 allocation of 4.0 GB per vCPU. The processor includes 54 MB of L3 cache, 1 MB of L2 cache per core, and 48 KB of L1 data cache. Hardware instruction support spans AVX, AVX-512 (including AVX-512 VNNI), AES, VAES, and SHA-NI cryptographic extensions. The instance carries no bundled local storage, requiring network-attached storage, and includes no dedicated GPUs.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong parallel throughput driven by the high core count. The system achieves strong performance tiers in multi-core metrics, including a stress-ng multi-core score of 120,717.34, a Geekbench multi-core score of 16,975.0, and a PassMark CPU score of 84,204.45. Cryptographic throughput and ray tracing reach top-tier percentiles, registering 104,777.43 in PassMark CPU encryption and 106,453.0 in Geekbench ray tracing. Memory bandwidth shows robust capabilities, exceeding 309 GB/sec for uncached read operations and 135 GB/sec for writes. Conversely, single-core benchmarks remain in the middle 50% average range, reflecting standard per-core execution speeds rather than ultra-high frequency compute.

Resource efficiency is optimal when processing large parallel pipelines, in-memory databases, and high-concurrency enterprise workloads. In application tests, it handles 107.15 million Redis SET operations per second and 66.2 GB/sec in static web serving throughput. CPU-based LLM inference is competitive for small and medium model prompt processing, but large 70B model text generation drops into the bottom 25% due to the lack of hardware accelerators. Given the scale of 128 vCPUs and 512 GB of RAM without local NVMe or GPUs, the instance is targeted at horizontally scaled web tiers, Clang-based compilation workflows, distributed cache clusters, and enterprise batch processing pipelines.
description: Google Cloud Platform n2-standard-128 is a general-purpose cloud instance equipped with 128 vCPUs (64 physical cores) on an Intel Xeon x86_64 processor clocked at 2.6 GHz, alongside 512.0 GB of RAM. The instance incorporates 54 MB of L3 cache, hardware cryptographic acceleration via AES and SHA-NI, and vector extensions including AVX-512. It provides no onboard local storage or GPUs. Performance testing highlights strong multi-core execution, memory bandwidth exceeding 309 GB/sec uncached reads, and high concurrency throughput across compiling, Redis caching, and encryption workloads, while single-core scores remain average. The server is well positioned for enterprise-grade web serving, CI/CD compilation, distributed caching, and large batch analytics.
